subject: Post-call: pilot scope, prompt-evals & access next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Menon <priya.menon@aurora-systems.com>, Alex Johnson <ajohnson@aurora-systems.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: pilot scope, prompt-evals & access next steps

Thanks again for your time earlier — good conversation and clear alignment on the business case. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps to get the pilot running. Please review and flag anything we missed.

Key pain points you shared
- High false-positive rate in intent classification for customer support (estimated 18-22% today).
- Latency-sensitive flows: < 500ms P95 needed for live routing decisions.
- Cost sensitivity for high-volume chat (expecting ~1.2M messages/mo).

Primary goals for the 6-week POC
1) Reduce intent classification errors by >= 30% on the supplied prompt suite.
2) Demonstrate sustained inference P95 under 500ms with 95th percentile traffic profile.
3) Show feasible per-message cost reduction vs current provider (baseline TBD).

Scope and acceptance criteria
- Model family: open-architecture medium LLM (we suggested Redwood-Base-7B quantized) for the initial runs.
- Prompt set: we will run two prompt families (classification + rerank) across your 1,200 labeled examples and a live slice. Success if error reduction and latency targets met.
- Owner: Aurora product (Priya) + Redwood engagement lead (Marissa).

Timeline (proposed)
- Week 0 (this week): access + mutual action plan sign-off.
- Week 1: dataset + sample prompt ingestion, initial infra provisioning.
- Weeks 2–3: parallel batch evals and latency tuning.
- Week 4: live traffic pilot for 72 hours.
- Week 5–6: results review, cost modeling, and recommended next steps.

Access & setup asks (what we need from Aurora)
- S3 access read-only to the labeled dataset or secure download link (scoped user).
- Test account credentials or JWT for a staging instance to run live-slice tests.
- Allowed IP range for VPC peering (we can provide sample values).
- Point of contact for security questionnaire (SOC2 evidence) — if procurement will require it, let us know now.

Attachments: I attached a short PoC charter template and a sample CSV of initial prompts (aurora_prompt_sample_set_v1.csv).

Next steps
- Priya: confirm S3 or upload option and POC POC-staging contact by EOD Thursday.
- Alex: confirm which traffic slice (web chat vs in-app) you want live-tested.
- Ben & Karthik: we’ll need a short window for provisioning; I’ll follow up with exact instance sizes once Alex confirms traffic slice.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-minute sync if that’s easier.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Priya Menon <priya.menon@aurora-systems.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Johnson <ajohnson@aurora-systems.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: pilot scope, prompt-evals & access next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Dataset access: we can provide an S3 read-only prefix by Friday morning. I’ll share the IAM user and a short README about label schema.
2) Traffic slice: start with web chat (high volume, lower complexity). If that looks good, we’ll follow with in-app.
3) Latency target nuance: 500ms P95 for the inference call itself is fine, but our end-to-end SLA considers routing + enrichment — we’ll measure both. Can you confirm whether Redwood’s SDK supports client-side batching controls?
4) Security: procurement asked for a SOC2 summary and encryption detail (KMS/HSM). Can Ben share the SOC2 snapshot and a contact for a GCR?

Accept the proposed timeline — slight tweak that we won’t be able to allocate a staging JWT until Monday next week (internal approvals). If you can begin offline with the labeled CSV that’ll speed the Week 1 work.

Attachment: I uploaded an initial sample live-slice log (we’ll send the full dump after the S3 link).

Priya
Product Lead — Customer Experience | Aurora Systems
priya.menon@aurora-systems.com | +1 212-555-0114

Ben / Karthik — looping you in to start the provisioning work and to confirm security artefacts for procurement. Summary of what Priya committed to: S3 prefix + README by Friday AM, staging JWT early next week, web chat slice for initial live run.

Quick asks for Redwood infra team: 
- Can we provision a small dedicated pool (2x A10G equivalent) for Week 2 latency tuning and Week 4 live slice? If you want, we can start with a single machine for batch evals and scale to 2 for live.
- Prepare a SOC2 summary doc and KMS integration notes (Ben, you often have a one-pager we can attach to procurement).
- I’ve attached the PoC charter template; I’ll fill in owners once you confirm capacity.

Ben — can you reply with a target provisioning ETA and link to the SOC2 snapshot? Karthik — if you can run a brief parameter recommendation (quantization + batching defaults) for a 7B-class model against a 128-token prompt, that will speed Week 2.

If helpful I’ll set a 15-min internal kickoff for Monday to align infra -> engagement -> product.

Thanks — Marissa
